problem: Agree with the writer: ਸੁਨਉ (and the parallel ਗਾਉ) is first person singular, and the pauri goes on in the first person (ਭਏ, ਹਮਾਰੀ); our Hindi has commands (सुनो, गाओ). ਮਿਟੇ is past, so मिट गये, matching the English (all ailments have gone).
fix: साधुकी संगतिमें मैं हरिका नाम सुनता हूँ। साधु-संगतिमें मैं हरिके गुण गाता हूँ। साधुकी संगतिमें (प्रभु) मनसे नहीं बिसरता। साधु-संगतिमें मनुष्य अवश्य पार उतरता है। साधुकी संगतिमें प्रभु मीठा लगता है। साधुकी संगतिमें वह घट-घटमें दिखायी देता है। साधु-संगतिमें हम (प्रभुके) आज्ञाकारी बने। साधु-संगतिमें हमारी मुक्ति हुई। साधुकी संगतिमें सब रोग मिट गये। हे नानक! साधुसे मिलन (ऊँचे) संयोगसे होता है।

problem: Agree with the writer: the verse says ਆਪਿ ਪਰਮੇਸੁਰ, himself the Supreme God; (का रूप) is a softening the verse does not have, and our Hindi of a08.p8 already says ब्रह्मज्ञानी सारी सृष्टिका कर्ता है without one.
fix: ब्रह्मज्ञानी ब्रह्मको जाननेवाला है। ब्रह्मज्ञानीका प्रेम एक (प्रभु) से है। ब्रह्मज्ञानी निश्चिन्त रहता है। ब्रह्मज्ञानीका उपदेश निर्मल है। ब्रह्मज्ञानी वही है जिसे प्रभु स्वयं बनाता है। ब्रह्मज्ञानीका बड़ा प्रताप है। ब्रह्मज्ञानीके दर्शन बड़े भाग्यसे मिलते हैं। ब्रह्मज्ञानीपर बार-बार बलिहारी जाना चाहिये। ब्रह्मज्ञानीको महेश्वर (शिव) भी खोजते हैं। हे नानक! ब्रह्मज्ञानी स्वयं परमेश्वर है।

problem: Agree with the writer: the verse says ਆਪਿ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰੁ; निराकार (का रूप), the form of the Formless, contradicts itself and is not in the verse. Matches the English (himself the Formless Lord).
fix: ब्रह्मज्ञानी सारी सृष्टिका कर्ता है। ब्रह्मज्ञानी सदा जीता है, मरता नहीं। ब्रह्मज्ञानी जीवको मुक्तिकी युक्ति देनेवाला है। ब्रह्मज्ञानी पूर्ण पुरुष और विधाता है। ब्रह्मज्ञानी अनाथोंका नाथ है। ब्रह्मज्ञानीका हाथ सबके ऊपर है। सारा आकार (सृष्टि) ब्रह्मज्ञानीका है। ब्रह्मज्ञानी स्वयं निराकार प्रभु है। ब्रह्मज्ञानीकी शोभा ब्रह्मज्ञानीको ही फबती है। हे नानक! ब्रह्मज्ञानी सबका स्वामी है।

problem: Agree with the writer: ਜਪੈ is third person present (the imperative would be ਜਪਿ / ਜਪਹੁ) and ਨਾਨਕ without aunkar is vocative, so the line is not a command; the last two lines read together, as in the English.
fix: स्वामी प्रभु सत्य है, सत्य है, सत्य है; गुरुकी कृपासे किसीने उसका बखान किया है। जिसने सब कुछ रचा, वह सच्चा है, सच्चा है, सच्चा है; करोड़ोंमें किसी विरलेने उसे पहचाना है। तेरा रूप भला है, भला है, भला है — अति सुन्दर, अपार और अनुपम। तेरी वाणी निर्मल है, निर्मल है, निर्मल है; घट-घटमें सुनी जाती है, कानोंसे सुनी और (मुखसे) बखानी जाती है। पवित्र, पवित्र, पवित्र और पुनीत वह है, हे नानक! जो मनमें प्रीति रखकर नाम जपता है।

problem: Lines 1, 3–6 and 9 are Sant Singh Khalsa's sentences with only the subject changed (centers his hopes on the One alone; is steeped in humility; delights in doing good to others; has no worldly entanglements; holds his wandering mind under control; In the Company of ..., all are saved): a run of his phrasing line after line, which the brief forbids even below 10 words. Same readings, own words; ਲੇ ... ਬੰਧਾ is caught and bound.
fix: The Brahm Giani places his hope in the One alone. The Brahm Giani never perishes. The Brahm Giani is filled with humility. The Brahm Giani is eager to do good to others. The Brahm Giani is not caught up in worldly affairs. The Brahm Giani catches the wandering mind and keeps it bound. To the Brahm Giani, whatever happens is good. The Brahm Giani is richly fruitful. In the Brahm Giani's company, everyone is saved. O Nanak, through the Brahm Giani the whole world remembers God.

problem: Inversion for effect (Of the Brahm Giani not even half a syllable can be spoken), against style.md §5; plain order reads better.
fix: The Brahm Giani's worth cannot be reckoned. The Brahm Giani holds everything within his mind. Who knows the secret of the Brahm Giani? To the Brahm Giani, salutations for ever. Not even half a syllable can be said about the Brahm Giani. The Brahm Giani is the Master of all. Who can tell the measure of the Brahm Giani? Only a Brahm Giani knows the state of a Brahm Giani. The Brahm Giani has no end and no limit. O Nanak, bow for ever to the Brahm Giani.

problem: Maya is not glossed anywhere in ashtapadi 9 (writer's own rule: once per ashtapadi; a07.p2 has the gloss).
fix: Ashtapadi. Falsehood does not touch his tongue. In his mind is love for the sight of the Immaculate Lord. His eyes do not gaze at the beauty of another's wife. He serves the Saadh, the holy one, and loves the company of the saints. His ears do not listen to slander of anyone. He considers himself the worst of all. By the Guru's grace he casts off the poison of Maya, the world's illusion and wealth. The desires of his mind depart from his mind. He has conquered his senses and is free of the five vices. O Nanak, among millions there is hardly one such Apras.

problem: Unclear: the reader is not told what the seed mantra is until later lines; our Hindi says it ((प्रभुका नाम ही) बीज-मन्त्र है), and lines 2 and 7 make it plain that the Naam is meant.
fix: The seed mantra, the Naam, is wisdom for all. Among the four castes, anyone may meditate on the Naam. Whoever meditates on it is liberated. In the Saadh's company, some rare person obtains it. By his grace, God enshrines it deep within the heart. It carries across even beasts, ghosts, fools and the stone-hearted. The Naam is the remedy for every ailment. Singing God's praises is the very form of well-being and joy. It is not obtained by any technique or by any religious rite. O Nanak, it is obtained by one for whom it was written from the beginning, by God's grace.

problem: the Ramdas reads as one particular person (or Guru Ram Das); the pauri defines a type of person, as with a Pandit, a Vaishnav.
fix: One in whose mind the Supreme Lord dwells: his name is truly Ramdas, the Lord's servant. The Lord, the Soul of all, has come into his sight. He has found him in the spirit of a servant of servants. He knows the Lord to be ever near, very near. Such a servant is accepted in the Lord's court. God himself shows grace to his servant. That servant comes to understand everything. Amid all, his soul stays detached. Such, O Nanak, is the way of a Ramdas.

problem: Lines 1 and 9 reword Sant Singh Khalsa sentence by sentence (One who, in his soul, loves the Will of God ...; Whatever God ordains, that is his way — overlap.py: 7 shared words, sentence nearly theirs).
fix: One who holds God's command dear in his soul is called Jivan Mukat, liberated while alive. To him joy is the same as sorrow. He is ever in bliss; there is no separation there. To him gold is the same as dust. Nectar is the same as bitter poison. Honour is the same as scorn. A beggar is the same as a king. Whatever God brings about, he takes as his way. O Nanak, that person is called Jivan Mukat.

problem: Lines 3–8 follow Sant Singh Khalsa sentence by sentence (know the essence of reality / the One alone / They become immortal; they live forever and ever / sing the ... of the Naam / They are absorbed in; overlap.py close 0.66, the highest in the batch). Also the beloved (singular form for they) is awkward.
fix: Millions upon millions are servants of the Supreme Lord; their souls are lit up. Millions upon millions are knowers of the essence; with their eyes they behold the One alone, always. Millions upon millions drink the nectar of the Naam; they have become deathless and live on for ever and ever. Millions upon millions sing the praises of the Naam; they are merged in the joy of the soul, in peace and poise. He keeps his servants in mind with every breath. O Nanak, they are dear to the Supreme God.

problem: Ambiguous subject: God is not named in the pauri, so after a human being and this man's hands, Whatever pleases him, that alone he does reads as the man doing what he likes, the opposite of the verse (ਜੋ ਤਿਸੁ ਭਾਵੈ = what pleases God). Also Maya unglossed in ashtapadi 11, and one / he switches for the same subject.
fix: Say, what can be achieved by a human being? Whatever pleases God, that he makes one do. If it were in this man's hands, he would seize everything. Whatever pleases God, that alone he does. Unknowing, one is engrossed in the poison of Maya, the world's illusion and wealth; if one knew, one would save oneself. Led astray by doubt, one runs in all ten directions; in an instant one goes round the four corners and comes back. Those to whom God, in his mercy, gives his devotion, O Nanak, merge in the Naam, God's Name.

problem: I do not agree that our Hindi is wrong here. ਨਾਨਕ has no aunkar, so it is vocative (the subject form is ਨਾਨਕੁ, as in a07.salok ਨਾਨਕੁ ਬਿਨਵੰਤਾ), and ਕਹੈ continues the subject of the whole pauri, the being (ਜਿਉ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਰਾਖੈ ਤਿਵ ਹੀ ਰਹੈ); our Hindi (हे नानक! गुरुकी कृपासे (वह) सच कहता है) has this. No Hindi change; the English should follow it. ਸਚੁ may also be the True One (one speaks of the True One); owner to decide. Note batch 01 a06.p5 (ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਸੁ ਕਹੈ) has the same pattern and should be made consistent.
fix: Sometimes one dances in many ways. Sometimes one stays asleep day and night. Sometimes one is fearsome in great anger. Sometimes one becomes the dust under everyone's feet. Sometimes one sits as a great king. Sometimes one wears the guise of a lowly beggar. Sometimes one falls into ill repute. Sometimes one is called good, very good. As God keeps one, so one remains. By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, one speaks the truth.

problem: Maya is not glossed anywhere in ashtapadi 12 (first occurrence here).
fix: As long as one thinks that anything can be done by him, he has no peace at all. As long as he thinks that he is the doer of anything, he wanders through wombs and births. As long as he holds one man as enemy and another as friend, his mind is not steady. As long as he is lost in attachment to Maya, the world's illusion and wealth, Dharam Rai punishes him. By God's grace the bonds break; by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, ego is shed.

problem: ਅਧਾਖੵਰੁ: current half a word | आधा अक्षर; the Hindi and the line mean half a letter, half a syllable.
fix: ਅਧਾਖੵਰੁ: आधा अक्षर | half a word / half a letter, half a syllable

problem: ਮ੍ਰਿਗਾਚ: the Hindi gives सिंह, the English lacks it; Skt mṛgāśana, deer-eater = lion (Monier-Williams).
fix: ਮ੍ਰਿਗਾਚ: मृग खानेवाले (सिंह) | tigers, predators / lions (deer-eaters)

problem: ਬਨਿ: English has only becoming; in ਸਾਧ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਬਨਿ ਆਈ (a07.p3) and ਸਾਧ ਕੀ ਸੋਭਾ ਸਾਧ ਬਨਿ ਆਈ (a07.p8) the line needs befitting / a bond formed (the Hindi फबकर has it).
fix: ਬਨਿ: बनकर, फबकर / (बनि आई) मेल बन गया | becoming / befitting, suiting; (with ਆਈ) has come to suit, a bond has formed
